dominant_strengths: Clean utilitarian header with confident sans-serif logotype and balanced nav spacing that feels professional and unfussy
Generous whitespace and clear content hierarchy let the showcased work be the star rather than competing with chrome
Tidy taxonomy row (Categories/Styles/Types/Subjects/Platforms) gives strong behavioral scaffolding for browsing
dominant_weaknesses: The single red dot logo mark is the only chromatic accent and feels arbitrary against an otherwise neutral palette, lacking systemic reuse
Hero headline typography is undersized relative to the massive carousel, weakening visceral impact and brand voice
Layout is conventional gallery-grid territory — little distinctiveness or signature gesture separates it from countless inspiration sites
fix_priorities: Scale up and tension the hero headline with an editorial type pairing to assert identity before the carousel dominates
Echo the red accent into interactive states, category chips, or pagination to make the palette feel intentional
Introduce a distinctive layout gesture (asymmetric overflow, custom transitions) to escape generic showcase-grid feel
Tighten carousel arrow controls and pagination dots — currently visually weak relative to the asset scale
rationale.norman_balance: Strong behavioral clarity and decent visceral polish, but reflective resonance is thin — nothing memorable to recount after leaving.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes, it functions as a credible curated gallery, but it reads as competent baseline rather than an inspiring showcase that itself inspires.
